log.explanation_raw: {"goal": "Find the marked item 11 among 4 items using only one call to the oracle (the 'checker').", "steps": [{"n": 1, "action": "First, a small correction: Grover's speedup is quadratic, not exponential. A classical search of N items needs about N checks; Grover needs about sqrt(N). For 4 items, one Grover check is enough. We start with both qubits as 0. Here |0> is the column vector [1, 0] and |1> is the column vector [0, 1]; two qubits written together, like |00>, mean both are 0.", "state": "|00>"}, {"n": 2, "action": "Apply H to both qubits: now all 4 items 00, 01, 10, 11 are in an equal mix, each with amplitude 1/2.", "state": "(|00> + |01> + |10> + |11>)/2"}, {"n": 3, "action": "The oracle checks each item and flips the sign of the marked one, 11. Probabilities do not change yet, only the sign.", "state": "(|00> + |01> + |10> - |11>)/2"}, {"n": 4, "action": "Diffusion: reflect every amplitude about the average. The amplitudes are 1/2, 1/2, 1/2, -1/2, so the average is 1/4. Each new amplitude is 2 x (1/4) minus the old one: the three unmarked items become 0 and the marked item becomes 1.", "state": "|11>"}, {"n": 5, "action": "Measure both qubits.", "state": "|11>"}], "final_result": "Measuring gives 11 with probability 1.0 after one Grover iteration; 00, 01 and 10 have probability 0.", "analogy": "Like a room of people where the one you want is told to step backward; then everyone is told to mirror their position around the group's average spot, which pushes the odd one far forward and the rest back to nothing.", "misconception": "Grover's speedup is quadratic (about sqrt(N) oracle queries instead of about N), not exponential.", "uncertain": []}
